content.title: Pay My Water & Trash Bill
content.summary: Residents of Arvada can pay their water and trash bills online, by phone, mail, or drop-box. For assistance with billing inquiries, including address changes or missed pickups, customers can contact utility billing at 720-898-7070. If water service has been shut off due to non-payment, full payment is required to restore service, and various support options are available for those facing financial difficulties.
content.body:
For address changes or service transfers please call customer service at 720-898-7070 (Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm). For missed recycling and trash pick up please call 720-898-7575. For additional utility bill questions, please submit a ticket through [Ask Arvada](/898) or [email us](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#aadfdec3c6cbcec7c3c4eacbd8dccbcecb84c5d8cd).

[Pay Online - now including AutoPay!](https://ipn.paymentus.com/cp/avdu)

**Note:**the prefilled amount under "amount due" may show charges that are not yet due. Please reference the amount on your bill statement for current charges.**If you pay the prefilled amount due, the difference will appear as a credit on your next billing statement.**The different amounts are related to how recycling and trash fees are entered into the billing system.

**[Water shut off](#shutoff):**See the information below if your water has been shut-off due to non-payment.

## Other Payment Options

1. [Automatic Payments](#tab3d3081e9-a95e-4e5b-b17f-aa7632ed2a4b_0)

**Auto-pay has moved online.**Visit the [**online payment portal**](https://ipn.paymentus.com/cp/avdu) tocreate an account or add auto-pay to your existing account. This service is available at no additional cost to customers. Visit the [Auto-Pay Update webpage](/1488) for more details and step-by-step instructions to sign up.

**Past due bill amounts:** If you have outstanding payments that are past due, please make a one-time payment. The past due amount will not auto-draw.

**Previous ACH auto-pay customer accounts** **were****canceled on Thursday, May 7, 2026.**Customers will need to re-enroll online or use a different payment method. Visit the [Auto-Pay Update webpage for more information](/1488). Auto-pay enrollment through the ACH form is no longer available.

1. [By Phone](#tab3d3081e9-a95e-4e5b-b17f-aa7632ed2a4b_1)

Call 720-898-7852 to make a credit card payment.

1. [By Mail](#tab3d3081e9-a95e-4e5b-b17f-aa7632ed2a4b_2)

Payment can be mailed to the utility billing office:

**8101 Ralston Road, Arvada, CO 80002**

Be sure to include your account number and/or property address.

1. [By Drop-Box](#tab3d3081e9-a95e-4e5b-b17f-aa7632ed2a4b_3)

Drop your payment in one of two drop boxes. Pay by**check or money order only.**

Locations:

- Post Office (5885 Allison Street) drive-thru
- City Hall (8101 Ralston Road) main entrance

## Bill support

Payment support options are available for Arvada customers.

- **Monthly equalized payments:**customers can choose a monthly equalized bill payment based upon the past 12 months of water consumption.
- **Payment plans**can be set up to repay overdue bills.
- **One time hardship credits** for qualifying customers.

Contact Utility Billing at 720-898-7070 for more information and support with bill payment.

### Water shut off

If your water service has been shut off due to lack of payment, payment must be made in full to restore water service. Payment options:

1. **Online**(available 24/7)
2. **By phone**at 720-898-7852 (available 24/7)
3. In person at City Hall, 8101 Ralston Road (available Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm)

**To schedule water service restoration,**call 720-898-7070 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm).

If you do not believe reasonable cause exists for suspension of service, you may submit a [Water Shutoff Review Request form](https://arvada-infrastructure.form.transform.civicplus.com/55407). This form must be completed online or at City Hall within 7 days of of the shutoff notice date.

### Outdoor water conservation

Small landscaping and habit changes can save a lot of water which reduces demand and can save money. Visit these resources for more information on how you can save:

- [Water saving programs](/602)
- [Outdoor watering tips](/597)

## About your services

The City’s water, sewer, storm and recycling / trash services are essential to Arvada’s health and safety. Each time you pay your bill, you’re investing in these critical services and ensuring you and your neighbors can continue to rely on them in the future.

The water, sewer, stormwater portion of your bill helps pay for operating, repairing and reinvesting in the complex systems that deliver treated, safe water and removes that water after use. Learn more on the [Utilities Transparency page](/661).

Your recycling / trash bill helps pay for the responsible disposal of your waste, protecting the health of our community and the environment. [Bulky Item](/728) and [Leaf Recycling](/718) events are available to all residents through this program.

### Current rates and fees

- [Water, sewer, stormwater rates and fees](/460), including water rates by usage tiers
- [Recycling and trash rates and fees](/715), including service levels and additional services
- [System Development Charges and meter fees](/1156)

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=32)

[How can I pay my water bill?](#)
:   Bills can be [paid online](https://ipn.paymentus.com/cp/avdu) by setting up an account. Options are also available to pay by phone, mail or drop box. Please visit the[Pay My Bill page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/453/Pay-My-Bill) for more information, including setting up automatic payments and paperless options.

[How can I report a water issue?](#)
:   If you notice or suspect problems in the water system, such as main breaks, service line leaks, frozen meters, low pressure, or dirty water, please notify us at 720-898-7070.

    To report a non-emergency water problem electronically, please use [Ask Arvada](https://seeclickfix.com/web_portal/m96AzqbgQ9RW9z5CcqFqEwP8/issues/map).

[How can I establish water and sewer service?](#)
:   **New Home Owners**: If you are a new homeowner here in Arvada, the title company you worked with during the purchase of your home will contact the City of Arvada to set up water / sewer service in your name.

    **Renters**: If you are a renter, your landlord will contact the City of Arvada to set up water/sewer service in your name.

[How can I get help paying my water bill?](#)
:   The Utility Billing Customer Service team is available to help customers navigate understanding and paying their bills. The City offers two programs to assist with bill payment:

    - **Payment plans** are available to create equalized payments across a 12 month period.
    - **One time hardship credits** are available for qualifying customers.

    Please call the Utility Billing team at 720-898-7070 for more information.

[What steps can I take to reduce my water bill amount?](#)
:   The City partners with [Resource Central](https://resourcecentral.org/) to offer several [outdoor water saving programs](https://www.arvadaco.gov/602/Water-Saving-Programs):

    - [Low-water garden plants (Garden in a Box)](https://resourcecentral.org/gardens/)
    - [Lawn replacement](https://resourcecentral.org/lawn/)
    - [Smart Controller](https://resourcecentral.org/slowtheflow/smartcontrollers/) sprinkler system upgrade
    - [Waterwise yard seminars](https://resourcecentral.org/seminars/)

    Additionally, read these [outdoor watering tips](https://www.arvadaco.gov/597/Watering-Tips) or watch this [video](https://youtu.be/2B3CWYNLrzE?si=Xwu-ozufc94GiJTV).

[What do my rates pay for?](#)
:   The rates and fees you pay can only be reinvested into the operation, maintenance, repair, and replacement needs of that system, nothing else. Here are some examples:

    **Water Service:**

    - Treatment and delivery of high-quality drinking water
    - Daily testing and monitoring to meet state and federal safety standards
    - Maintenance of over 600 miles of water pipes
    - Operation of two water treatment facilities

    **Wastewater Service:**

    - Collection and removal of wastewater from homes and businesses
    - Treatment through our partnership with Metro Water Recovery
    - Protection of public health and the environment
    - Maintenance of over 450 miles of wastewater pipes

    **Stormwater Service:**

    - Management of stormwater runoff from rain and snowmelt
    - Flood protection for homes and businesses
    - Water quality protection for local streams and waterways
    - Maintenance of over 220 miles of storm pipes and open channels

    Revenue from utility rates is reinvested directly into these systems—not into the City's general fund or other services.

[Why do water rates increase?](#)
:   Water rates increase year over year to manage our aging infrastructure, much of which was built between the 60s to 80s, keep up with inflation and general maintenance and repairs as needed. The City continually invests in our infrastructure to continue to deliver clean, reliable drinking water and dispose of wastewater after use.

    Just like homeownership, over time the City must make substantial investments to maintain, repair and replace parts of our water and sewer systems. Increases in rates and fees will help to fund the necessary reinvestment in these systems to ensure we continue to provide the level of service our customers have come to expect.

    Additional factors include:

    - Our partnerships with Denver Water for about 75% of our water supply and Metro Water Recovery for wastewater treatment. These organizations also increase rates each year which are passed along to customers.
    - We also raise System Development Charges (SDC) to make sure growth pays for itself in Arvada.  SDCs are paid by new development to fund projects that add system capacity so our existing businesses and residents do not.

[When will I see increases on my bill?](#)
:   Rate and fee increases will be reflected beginning with your **first bill of the year.** Customers across Arvada receive their bills at different times. Every customer pays for 365 days of water at the rate for that year. The bill reflects the 8 weeks of water use, prior to the bill date.

    Please watch the [Understanding Your Utility Bill video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QBaw7GsnCzM) or visit the [Rates and Fees webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/460/Rates-and-Fees) for more information.

[Are rate increases because of new development in Arvada?](#)
:   No, the City of Arvada is committed to a philosophy that growth pays for itself. This means that customer rates and fees pay for the necessary reinvestment in the repair, replacement and maintenance of existing water and wastewater systems. Developers pay System Development Charges (SDC) when they connect new homes and businesses to our existing system. These charges help cover the investment in expanding the capacity of our water and wastewater system. Learn more on the [Utilities Transparency webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/661/Utilities-Transparency).

[Does Arvada have outdoor watering restrictions?](#)
:   The City receives the majority of its water supply from Denver Water. We are contractually required to follow drought related water restrictions in line with Denver Water. Visit the [water restrictions webpage](/1499) for more information, including any current restrictions.

    Small landscaping and habit changes can save water which reduces demand and can save money. Visit the [Outdoor Watering Tips page](/597) for helpful information.

[Do I need water / sewer line insurance for my home?](#)
:   Private water / sewer line insurance is not required by the City of Arvada. [City Code section 102.76](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH102UT_ARTIIWASE_DIV3WASU_S102-76MASELI) states that property owners are responsible for the portion of the service line located on their property. Property owners should make their own decisions regarding insurance needs.

    Insurance companies may occasionally advertise services to property owners. These companies are not associated with the City of Arvada.

/FAQ.aspx
